cases.body: Metropolitan Council (BL2026-1489, sponsor Rollin Horton, D20); Metro Government would acquire by negotiation or condemnation
cases.purpose: Acquire the fee interest in a 23.49-acre parcel at 648 Grassmere Park (Parcel 13300013500) for Metro 'office, warehouse, training and other uses' (mayor's office lists Elections Office, NDOT, Schools Hands On Science program)
cases.serves_data_center_quote: Taking is OF a DC Blox data-center site FOR municipal use; the council vote was explicitly to stop a data center next to the zoo ('We're looking at every tool in the toolbox to try to stop this data center from being built right next to our zoo')
cases.status: Passed third reading 27-5 (roll call), as amended, per Council Watch tracker. First reading 2026-07-07 (voice vote); second 2026-07-21 (27-3). Mayor's office: vote 'does not commit Metro to buying the land'; appraisal before negotiation; a judge could set price if no agreement. Not yet acquired.
cases.response: Mayor's office and council members opposed to the DC Blox site; zoo leadership and nearby residents objected to noise, emissions, lighting. Two challenges to the zoning administrator's land-use designation are pending at the Board of Zoning Appeals (per WSMV).
cases.verbatim: Authorizing The Metropolitan Government to acquire the fee interest in a parcel of property; for office, warehouse, training and other uses.
cases.source_title: Metro Council Watch tracker, BL2026-1489 (third-party transcription of council record; Legistar not reachable)
cases.notes: Probe HIT on both quotes. Vote tally and reading dates come from a third-party tracker, not Legistar; Legistar and the ordinance text still need a direct read before shipping. Media (WSMV 2026-08-05, Fox17, Axios) confirm the passage and the condemnation-or-negotiation authority. Do not record as a data-center taking: the public use is municipal.

cases.jurisdiction: Loudoun County, Virginia (Golden-to-Mars 500 kV / 230 kV reliability loop)
cases.body: Virginia SCC (route order); Dominion Energy (utility; condemnation as delegated power). The SCC said it cannot authorize condemnation of land owned by LCPS for Dominion's purposes; Loudoun County Public Schools land is the contested parcel
cases.purpose: Golden-to-Mars transmission line and substation upgrades (Golden, Mars, Prentice Drive, Sojourner, Shellhorn); reliability loop feeding Data Center Alley, Ashburn
cases.serves_data_center_quote: Dominion spokesperson: the project is 'essential to support homes, businesses, schools, hospitals, public safety facilities, data centers, and other customers' (data-center link is Dominion's own wording, not a Dominion-only load attribution)
cases.event_date: 2026-06-29 (SCC final order, Route 3A per Dominion project page; WJLA quotes Supervisor Umstattd citing the 6/29/2026 final order)
cases.status: SCC final order issued 2026-06-29 approving Route 3A. School Board and LVE HOA reconsideration motions denied. No condemnation filing found. Rep. Subramanyam urged SCC to consider three new routes (2026-10-13 per Loudoun coverage).
cases.response: Loudoun County Board of Supervisors joined reconsideration; School Board and Loudoun Valley Estates HOA opposed the route; Umstattd: the SCC cannot authorize condemnation for Dominion of LCPS land.
cases.verbatim: 6/29/2026 final order; essential to support homes, businesses, schools, hospitals, public safety facilities, data centers, and other customers
cases.source_title: WJLA (7News), Loudoun homeowners appear to lose battle with Dominion's data center transmission lines, July 2026
cases.notes: Probe HIT on both quotes. The 6/29 date is from a county supervisor's statement; the SCC docket number (PUR-2025-?) is not confirmed. The 'essential ... data centers' sentence is Dominion's own statement, which supports a stated link but not a load-attribution split. Separate from the Aspen-Golden line (SCV affirmed 2026-02-19). Condemnation filings for Golden-to-Mars: none found; the SCC's docket system is needed. Not yet a LandTaking record: no condemnation has been filed on what we found.

IURC Cause No. 46394 (AES Indiana, Google data center, Monrovia/Morgan County). Approval reported by DCD and New Project Media; ~10-mile 345 kV line from Antioch to Blue Bluff substations; CAC testimony filed 2026-06-22. Approval date and line-route eminent domain status not confirmed. One fetch of Inside Indiana Business was refused by the tool, so this is a lead, not a verified case. Next: the IURC order and the AES project page.

PPL plans ~9 miles of 230 kV line across Lycoming and Union counties; residents link it to PNK Group's Great Stream Commons data center in Gregg Twp; PPL has not confirmed the link. Construction awaits PA PUC approval (winter 2027 start). No PUC docket number found in search. Next: PUC eFiling search for PPL filings in Union/Lycoming. Eminent-domain status unknown.

Nebraska LB 1261 reported enacted (signed 2026-04-14 per a state report) limiting public utilities from taking privately owned generation by eminent domain. Search snippet only; not fetched from the bill page. Verify on nebraskalegislature.gov before using. Same report names LB 1010 (eminent domain for energy storage, enactment unconfirmed).

Maryland SB 1000 (2026RS), transmission line and data center provisions: Senate page shows first reading only in Rules, so not enacted per these results. Do not treat as an eminent-domain limit without reading the bill text.
South Dakota HJR 5001, proposed constitutional amendment restricting eminent domain, passed House 62-5; no later action found. Not a data-center-specific bill; note only.
PA HB 710 (the lead named in the spec is Ohio HB 710, and a Pennsylvania number was not located), Ohio HB 710, Texas, and Virginia bill status: search returned nothing. Not verified.
